title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Vertex-sharing of mixed hydroxo building blocks is a general way to increase structural diversity, and the clusters above nuclearity 20 that are drawn from these mixed-motif families are typically supported by template anions.
explanation: Examples include Ln11, Ln12 and Ln19 from trigonal bipyramids plus cubanes; Ln48 from cubanes plus square pyramids; Ln14 from octahedra plus square pyramids; Ln72 from triangles plus square pyramids; and Ln26, Ln27, Ln36 and Ln37 from cubanes plus triangles. The authors explicitly call mixed vertex-sharing an effective synthetic strategy and tie nuclearities above 20 in Figs. 20 and 21 to template anions.
scope: Lanthanide hydroxide clusters assembled from two different basic polyhedra.
caveats: Some lower-nuclearity mixed-motif clusters (Ln11–Ln19, Ln14) are listed alongside the templated giants, so mixed building blocks alone do not guarantee nuclearity above 20.
